Name: AllowDatagramProcessingOnWinServer
Control Name: This setting controls datagram processing for Network Protection is enabled on Server
Description: Controls datagram processing for Network Protection on Windows Server. Enables network-level protection against web-based threats.
Security Impact: Disabling removes network-layer threat protection, exposing the server to web-based attacks and malicious network traffic.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Disabling reduces defense-in-depth; verify no third-party network protection replaces it.

Name: AllowNetworkProtectionOnWinServer
Control Name: This setting controls whether Network Protection is allows to be configured into block or Audit mode on Windows Server
Description: Enables Microsoft Defender Network Protection on Windows Server, blocking connections to malicious domains and IPs.
Registry Key: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection" -Name "AllowNetworkProtectionOnWinServer"
Security Impact: Disabling removes DNS/IP reputation blocking, allowing connections to known malicious endpoints.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Disabling weakens network threat protection; may be needed if third-party proxy/firewall handles this.

Name: ASRBlockAbuseOfExploitedVulnerableSignedDrivers
Control Name: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
Description: ASR rule that blocks applications from writing vulnerable signed drivers to disk, preventing kernel-level exploits.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5"
Security Impact: Disabling allows exploitation of vulnerable signed drivers for kernel-level privilege escalation.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H - Disabling exposes to driver-based exploits; audit mode recommended for initial deployment.

Name: ASRBlockAdobeReaderFromCreatingChildProcesses
Control Name: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes
Description: ASR rule that prevents Adobe Reader from creating child processes, blocking PDF-based malware execution chains.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c"
Security Impact: Disabling allows PDF documents to launch arbitrary processes via Adobe Reader.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Server environments rarely use Adobe Reader; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRBlockEXEFromEmailClientAndWebmail
Control Name: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Description: ASR rule that blocks executable content from email clients and webmail, preventing email-based malware delivery.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "be9ba2d9-53ea-4cdc-84e5-9b1eeee46550"

Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Servers typically do not run email clients; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRBlockEXEFromRunningUnlessTrusted

Description: ASR rule that blocks executables from running unless they meet prevalence, age, or trusted list criteria.

Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:M - May block legitimate but uncommon tools; test in audit mode first.

Name: ASRBlockJSVBSLaunchingDownloadedContent
Control Name: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content
Description: ASR rule that blocks JavaScript and VBScript from launching downloaded executable content.

Security Impact: Disabling allows script-based download-and-execute attack chains.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Server workloads rarely depend on JS/VBS downloading executables.

Name: ASRBlockLSASSCredentialStealing

Name: ASRBlockOfficeApplicationsFromCreatingChildProcesses

Name: ASRBlockOfficeFromCreatingExecutableContent

Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Servers rarely run Office; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRBlockOfficeFromInjectingCodeIntoProcesses

Description: ASR rule that blocks Office applications from injecting code into other processes.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "75668c1f-73b5-4cf0-bb93-3ecf5cb7cc84"
Security Impact: Disabling allows Office-based process injection attacks.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Servers rarely run Office; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRBlockPersistenceThroughWMIEventSubscription

Description: ASR rule that blocks persistence mechanisms using WMI event subscriptions, a common living-off-the-land technique.

Security Impact: Disabling allows attackers to establish persistent footholds via WMI event subscriptions.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:H - Blocking may affect legitimate monitoring tools using WMI subscriptions.

Name: ASRBlockPotentiallyObfuscatedScripts
Control Name: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts
Description: ASR rule that blocks execution of potentially obfuscated scripts, detecting and preventing script-based evasion.

Security Impact: Disabling allows obfuscated malicious scripts to execute without inspection.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:M - May flag legitimate encoded scripts; test in audit mode first.

Name: ASRBlockProcessCreationFromPSExecAndWMICommands
Control Name: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands
Description: ASR rule that blocks process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands. Baseline sets Audit (2) for Azure Local because LCM depends on WMI orchestration.

Security Impact: Setting to Block (1) prevents WMI-based remote process creation, breaking lifecycle management orchestration.
Change Risk Level: Func:Critical / Sec:M - Setting to Block breaks remote management tools that rely on WMI; keep as Audit on managed servers.

Name: ASRBlockRebootingMachineInSafeMode
Control Name: Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode (preview)
Description: ASR rule that blocks processes from rebooting the machine into Safe Mode, preventing attackers from disabling security controls.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "33ddedf1-c6e0-47cb-833e-de6133960387"
Security Impact: Disabling allows malware to reboot into Safe Mode where security tools are disabled.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Minimal operational impact; Safe Mode reboots are rarely needed in production.

Name: ASRBlockUntrustedAndUnsignedProcessesRunningFromUSB
Control Name: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB
Description: ASR rule that blocks untrusted and unsigned processes from running from USB removable drives.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "b2b3f03d-6a65-4f7b-a9c7-1c7ef74a9ba4"
Security Impact: Disabling allows execution of untrusted code from removable media.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Server environments rarely use USB drives; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRBlockUseOfCopiedOrImpersonatedSystemTools
Control Name: Block use of copied or impersonated system tools (preview)
Description: ASR rule that blocks use of copied or impersonated system tools, preventing living-off-the-land binary (LOLBin) abuse.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "c0033c00-d16d-4114-a5a0-dc9b3a7d2ceb"
Security Impact: Disabling allows attackers to use renamed copies of system tools to evade detection.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:M - May affect legitimate admin tools if they copy system binaries; test in audit mode.

Name: ASRBlockWebshellCreationForServers
Control Name: Block Webshell creation for Servers
Description: ASR rule that blocks webshell creation on servers, preventing web-based backdoor deployment.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "a8f5898e-1dc8-49a9-9878-85004b8a61e6"
Security Impact: Disabling allows creation of webshell files that provide persistent remote access to attackers.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H - Critical server protection; webshells are a primary post-exploitation technique.

Name: ASRBlockWIN32APIFromOfficeMacros
Control Name: Block Win32 API calls from Office macros
Description: ASR rule that blocks Win32 API calls from Office macros, preventing advanced macro-based attacks.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "92e97fa1-2edf-4476-bdd6-9dd0b4dddc7b"
Security Impact: Disabling allows Office macros to call Win32 APIs for system-level operations.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Servers rarely run Office macros; minimal operational impact.

Name: ASRUseAdvancedProtectionAgainstRansomware
Control Name: Use advanced protection against ransomware
Description: ASR rule that enables advanced heuristic protection against ransomware behavior patterns.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules" -Name "c1db55ab-c21a-4637-bb3f-a12568109d35"
Security Impact: Disabling removes ransomware-specific behavioral detection, relying only on signature-based protection.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H - Critical anti-ransomware layer; disabling significantly increases ransomware risk.

Name: AttackSurfaceReductionRules
Control Name: Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules
Description: Master configuration for Attack Surface Reduction rules. Controls whether individual ASR rules are enabled, audited, or disabled.
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR" -Name "ExploitGuard_ASR_Rules"
Security Impact: Disabling removes all ASR protections at once, eliminating a critical defense-in-depth layer.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:H - Master switch for all ASR rules; disabling removes multiple security protections simultaneously.

Name: DisableAntiSpyware
Control Name: Turn off Microsoft Defender AntiVirus
Description: Controls whether Microsoft Defender Antivirus is enabled. Must be 0 (enabled) to provide antimalware protection.
Security Impact: Enabling this setting (value 1) completely disables Microsoft Defender AV, removing all malware protection.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:Critical - Disabling the antivirus engine removes all real-time and scan-based malware protection.

Name: DisableAutoExclusions
Control Name: Turn off Auto Exclusions
Description: Controls automatic exclusions for server roles. When enabled, Defender automatically excludes files/paths for detected server roles.
Security Impact: Disabling auto-exclusions may cause performance impact on server workloads or false positives on role-specific files.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:L - Auto-exclusions are a performance optimization; disabling increases scan coverage but may impact performance.

Name: DisableBehaviorMonitoring
Control Name: Turn on behavior monitoring
Description: Controls real-time behavior monitoring for suspicious process activity patterns.
Security Impact: Disabling removes behavioral detection of fileless malware and living-off-the-land attacks.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H - Behavioral monitoring catches threats that signature-based detection misses.

Name: DisableBlockAtFirstSeen
Control Name: Configure the 'Block at First Sight' feature
Description: Controls Block at First Seen (BAFS), which uses cloud intelligence to block new malware within seconds of first detection.
Security Impact: Disabling removes rapid cloud-based verdict for unknown files, increasing window of exposure to zero-day threats.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Requires cloud connectivity; disconnected environments cannot use this feature.

Name: DisableEmailScanning
Control Name: Turn on e-mail scanning
Description: Controls scanning of email files (PST, DBX, MBX) by the Defender scan engine.
Security Impact: Disabling prevents detection of malware stored in email archives on the server.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Most servers do not store email locally; impact depends on workload.

Name: DisableIOAVProtection
Control Name: Scan all downloaded files and attachments
Description: Controls scanning of all downloaded files and attachments (IOAV = Internet Originated Attachment/Volume).
Security Impact: Disabling removes automatic scanning of files downloaded from the internet.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Important for servers that download content; less relevant for isolated infrastructure.

Name: DisableRealtimeMonitoring
Control Name: Turn off real-time protection
Description: Controls real-time file access scanning. Must be 0 (enabled) for continuous malware protection.
Security Impact: Disabling removes all real-time file scanning, allowing malware to execute without detection.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:Critical - Real-time protection is the primary defense layer; disabling creates critical exposure.

Name: DisableRemovableDriveScanning
Control Name: Scan removable drives
Description: Controls scanning of removable drives (USB) during full scans.
Security Impact: Disabling prevents detection of malware on removable media during scans.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Server environments rarely use removable drives; minimal impact.

Name: DisableRoutinelyTakingAction
Control Name: Turn off routine remediation
Description: Controls whether Defender automatically remediates detected threats or requires manual action.
Security Impact: Enabling prevents automatic remediation, leaving detected threats active until manually addressed.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Manual remediation increases response time; automatic action is preferred for servers.

Name: DisableScanOnUpdate
Control Name: Turn on scan after security intelligence update
Description: Controls whether a scan is triggered after a security intelligence (signature) update.
Security Impact: Disabling prevents immediate scanning with new signatures, delaying detection of newly-identified threats.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Scheduled scans still occur; post-update scan is an additional detection opportunity.

Name: DisableScriptScanning
Control Name: Turn on script scanning
Description: Controls real-time scanning of scripts (PowerShell, VBScript, JavaScript) during execution.
Security Impact: Disabling removes script-level malware detection, a critical vector for fileless attacks.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H - Script scanning is essential for detecting PowerShell-based attacks on servers.

Name: DisallowExploitProtectionOverride
Control Name: Prevent users from modifying settings
Description: Prevents users from modifying Exploit Protection settings, ensuring centrally managed mitigations remain enforced.
Registry Key: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender Security Center\App and Browser protection
Validation: Run Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender Security Center\App and Browser protection" -Name "DisallowExploitProtectionOverride"
Security Impact: Allowing overrides lets users weaken exploit mitigations on individual applications.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Administrative setting; minimal operational impact.

Name: EnableConvertWarnToBlock
Control Name: Convert warn verdict to block
Description: Converts Network Protection warn verdicts to block actions, enforcing stricter network filtering.
Security Impact: Disabling allows users to bypass network protection warnings and access potentially malicious sites.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Strengthens network protection; minimal operational impact on servers.

Name: EngineRing
Control Name: Select the channel for Microsoft Defender monthly engine updates
Description: Controls the update ring for the Defender antimalware engine, determining how quickly engine updates are received.
Security Impact: Changing to a slower ring delays engine updates, potentially missing protection improvements.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Update ring selection is an operational choice; production servers typically use stable ring.

Name: HideExclusionsFromLocalAdmins
Control Name: Control whether or not exclusions are visible to Local Admins
Description: Hides configured scan exclusions from local administrators, preventing exclusion discovery for evasion.
Security Impact: Showing exclusions allows attackers to discover safe paths for placing malware.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Security hardening; may complicate legitimate troubleshooting of exclusion issues.

Name: HideExclusionsFromLocalUsers
Control Name: Control whether exclusions are visible to local users
Description: Hides configured scan exclusions from standard users, preventing exclusion discovery.
Security Impact: Showing exclusions to users allows potential discovery of unmonitored paths.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Standard users should not see security configuration details.

Name: LocalSettingOverrideSpynetReporting
Control Name: Configure local setting override for reporting to Microsoft MAPS
Description: Controls whether local policy can override cloud protection (MAPS) reporting settings.
Security Impact: Allowing local overrides lets individual machines opt out of cloud-based threat intelligence sharing.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Administrative enforcement setting; minimal operational impact.

Name: MpCloudBlockLevel
Control Name: Select cloud protection level
Description: Sets the aggressiveness of cloud-based blocking. Higher levels increase detection but may cause more false positives.
Security Impact: Lowering the cloud block level reduces detection of emerging threats from cloud intelligence.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Higher levels may cause false positives; balance with workload requirements.

Name: OobeEnableRtpAndSigUpdate
Control Name: Configure real-time protection and Security Intelligence Updates during OOBE
Description: Enables real-time protection and signature updates during the Out of Box Experience (OOBE), ensuring protection from first boot.
Security Impact: Disabling leaves the system unprotected during initial setup, creating a window of vulnerability.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Only affects initial deployment; production servers are past OOBE.

Name: PlatformRing
Control Name: Select the channel for Microsoft Defender monthly platform updates
Description: Controls the update ring for the Defender platform, determining how quickly platform updates are received.
Security Impact: Changing to a slower ring delays platform updates and new feature availability.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Update ring selection is an operational choice.

Name: PUAProtection
Control Name: Configure detection for potentially unwanted applications
Description: Enables detection and blocking of Potentially Unwanted Applications (PUA) such as adware and bundleware.
Security Impact: Disabling allows PUA software to install without detection or blocking.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - PUA is less relevant on servers but provides defense-in-depth.

Name: QuickScanIncludeExclusions
Control Name: Scan excluded files and directories during quick scans
Description: Controls whether quick scans also scan files in exclusion paths, providing additional coverage.
Security Impact: Excluding these paths from quick scans reduces scan coverage.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Quick scan scope adjustment; full scans still cover all paths.

Name: SchedulerRandomizationTime
Control Name: Configure scheduled task times randomization window
Description: Sets the randomization window (in hours) for scheduled scan start times to avoid all machines scanning simultaneously.
Security Impact: No randomization causes all machines to scan at the same time, potentially causing resource spikes.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Performance optimization; no security impact.

Name: SignaturesRing
Control Name: Select the channel for Microsoft Defender daily security intelligence updates
Description: Controls the update ring for signature/security intelligence updates.
Security Impact: Slower ring delays signature updates, increasing the window of exposure to newly identified threats.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Update ring selection; production typically uses stable ring.

Name: SpynetReporting
Control Name: Join Microsoft MAPS
Description: Controls Microsoft MAPS (cloud protection) membership level. Advanced membership provides enhanced cloud-based protection.
Security Impact: Disabling MAPS removes cloud-based threat intelligence, relying only on local signatures.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M - Cloud intelligence significantly improves detection; required for Block at First Seen.

Name: SubmitSamplesConsent
Control Name: Send file samples when further analysis is required
Description: Controls automatic sample submission to Microsoft for cloud analysis. Safe samples (no PII) are sent by default.
Security Impact: Disabling prevents cloud-based deep analysis of suspicious files.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L - Required for full cloud protection; disconnected environments cannot use this.

Name: ConfigureSystemGuardLaunch
Control Name: Secured-Core SystemGuard (DRTM)
Description: Enables System Guard Secure Launch (DRTM) to protect boot from firmware attacks.
Security Impact: Without DRTM, firmware attacks can compromise the security chain before OS loads.
Change Risk Level: Low - Enables hardware-based root of trust (DRTM); no application compatibility impact

Name: EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity
Control Name: Secured-Core Virtualization Based Security (VBS)
Description: Enables Virtualization Based Security (VBS) to isolate critical OS components.
Security Impact: Disabling VBS removes memory isolation for credentials and code integrity.
Change Risk Level: Low - Enables Virtualization Based Security; foundational for Credential Guard and HVCI with minimal operational risk

Name: HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity
Control Name: Secured-Core Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI)
Description: Enables Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) for kernel-mode code signing.
Security Impact: Disabling HVCI allows unsigned kernel drivers, increasing rootkit exposure.
Change Risk Level: Low - Enforces kernel-mode code integrity via hypervisor; may block unsigned/incompatible drivers

Name: HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrityStatus
Control Name: Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI)

Control Name: Secure boot state

Name: AfdDisableAddressSharing
Control Name: System Services Afd DisableAddressSharing
Description: Configures 'System Services Afd DisableAddressSharing' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Hardens the Ancillary Function Driver (AFD) by disabling socket address sharing, reducing local socket-hijacking opportunities.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:H — Network stack setting; affects socket sharing behavior

Name: AllowAnonymousSIDOrNameTranslation
Control Name: Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation
Description: Controls the 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' right, limiting it to authorized accounts to reduce attack surface.
Security Impact: Disables anonymous SID-to-name translation, preventing unauthenticated callers from mapping SIDs to account names for reconnaissance. Re-enabling translation hands unauthenticated callers a SID-to-name enumeration surface for reconnaissance.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H — Anonymous access control; changing exposes enumeration surface

Name: AllowCustomSSPAPIntoLSASS
Control Name: Allow Custom SSPs and APs to be loaded into LSASS
Description: Controls loading of custom Security Support Providers into LSASS.
Security Impact: Restricts loading of custom security packages into LSASS, reducing the chance of malicious authentication packages harvesting credentials. Allowing custom packages back into LSASS reopens a path for malicious authentication packages to harvest credentials.
Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:H — LSA process protection; changing may affect credential providers

Name: AllowedToFormatAndEjectRemovableMedia
Control Name: Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media
Description: Configures 'Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Restricts which users may format and eject removable media interactively, limiting console-side data-handling to authorized roles. Widening the allowed set lets unauthorized console users format or eject media holding system data.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L — Removable-media policy; no cluster service dependency

Name: AllowICMPRedirectOverrideOSPF
Control Name: Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes
Description: Configures 'Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Legacy MSS network/kernel hardening '(EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes'. Tightens older TCP/IP and DLL-search behaviors (source routing, NetBIOS name release, DLL search order) to the recommended safer values. Reverting to the legacy values re-enables ICMP-redirect route injection and related TCP/IP spoofing weaknesses.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M — Network protocol setting; standard hardening

Name: AllowLocalSystemNULLSessionFallback
Control Name: Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback
Description: Configures 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Disables NULL-session fallback for the LocalSystem account (set to 0), so LocalSystem can no longer fall back to unauthenticated null-credential NTLM sessions. This removes an anonymous authentication path that could be used for credential-less enumeration or relay. Re-enabling fallback restores that anonymous NTLM path for credential-less enumeration or relay.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H — NULL session fallback; changing exposes anonymous access surface

Name: AllowLocalSystemToUseComputerIdentityForNTLM
Control Name: Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM
Description: Configures 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Configures whether Local System uses the computer identity for NTLM, ensuring consistent, expected service authentication behavior. Disabling it lets LocalSystem fall back to anonymous outbound NTLM, weakening service authentication assurance.
Change Risk Level: Func:H / Sec:H — Authentication protocol change may break inter-node cluster auth

Name: AllowPKU2UAuthenticationAllowOnlineID
Control Name: Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities
Description: Configures 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Allows this computer to accept PKU2U authentication requests that use online identities (the baseline sets AllowOnlineID to 1). Although STIG/CIS historically disable PKU2U, this baseline intentionally enables it because failover clustering relies on PKU2U for node-to-node authentication using Microsoft-trusted online identities. Setting it to 0 would confine authentication to domain/AD identities and can break cluster node communication and other online-identity peer logons.
Change Risk Level: Func:Critical / Sec:H — PKU2U is required by Cluster, and additionally for AD-less deployments; disabling breaks cluster authentication

Name: AllowSystemToBeShutDownWithoutHavingToLogOn
Control Name: Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on
Description: Configures 'Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Controls whether the host can be shut down from the logon screen without authenticating, limiting unauthenticated denial-of-availability at the console. Enabling shutdown-without-logon lets anyone at the console power off the host, an unauthenticated availability risk.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L — Console-shutdown policy; no cluster functional impact

Name: AllowUIAccessApplicationsToPromptForElevation
Control Name: User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop
Description: Configures 'User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: User Account Control control 'User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop'. Maintains admin-approval elevation, secure-desktop prompting, installer detection, or token filtering that constrains silent privilege elevation by malware. Relaxing it allows UIAccess apps to prompt off the secure desktop, weakening protection against elevation spoofing.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:M — UAC elevation prompt behavior; no cluster functional impact

Name: AppCompatTurnOffProgramInventory
Control Name: Turn off Inventory Collector
Description: Configures 'Turn off Inventory Collector' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.

Name: BlockConsumerMicrosoftAccounts

Name: BlockNetbiosDiscovery

Name: BlockNTLM
Control Name: Block NTLM (LM NTLM NTLMv2)
Description: Configures 'Block NTLM (LM NTLM NTLMv2)' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: NTLM-blocking control 'Block NTLM (LM NTLM NTLMv2)'. Constrains or blocks NTLM so Kerberos is preferred, reducing NTLM relay and credential-replay exposure; exception lists scope where NTLM remains permitted. Relaxing the block restores broad NTLM use and its relay and credential-replay exposure.
Change Risk Level: Func:H / Sec:H — Authentication protocol change may break inter-node cluster auth

Name: BlockNTLMServerExceptionList
Control Name: Block NTLM Server Exception List
Description: Configures 'Block NTLM Server Exception List' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.

Name: ConfigureSMBV1Server

Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:M — SMB config change may affect storage or file sharing operations

Name: CryptographyAllowedKerberosEncryptionTypes

Name: DeviceGuardLsaCfgFlags
Control Name: Turn on CredentialGuard
Description: Configures 'Turn on CredentialGuard' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.

Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:L — Toggle: CredentialGuard — Tested and offered via Enable/Disable-AzsSecurity

Name: DeviceGuardRequireMicrosoftSignedBootChain
Control Name: Secured-Core Require MicrosoftSignedBootChain
Description: Configures 'Secured-Core Require MicrosoftSignedBootChain' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires a Microsoft-signed UEFI Secure Boot chain as a Virtualization-Based Security prerequisite (1 enforces while the platform emits a Secure-Boot-compatible TCG log, 2 gates release of the VSM master key). Anchors the hardware root of trust for VBS, HVCI, and Credential Guard; 0 removes the requirement entirely.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H — VBS related settings — we do not support VBS disablement

Name: DeviceGuardRequirePlatformSecurityFeatures
Control Name: Secured-Core Require Platform Security (Secure Boot, DMA)
Description: Configures '"Secured-Core Require Platform Security (Secure Boot, DMA)"' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires platform security features before Virtualization-Based Security activates: Secure Boot (1), or Secure Boot with DMA protection (3). This establishes the hardware root of trust that VBS, HVCI, and Credential Guard depend on, and value 3 additionally blocks malicious DMA-capable peripherals from reading protected memory. A lower or cleared value lets VBS run without verified platform protections, weakening the isolation those features provide.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H — VBS related settings — we do not support VBS disablement

Name: DeviceGuardRequireUEFIMemoryAttributesTable
Control Name: Secured-Core Require UEFI Memory Attribute Table
Description: Configures 'Secured-Core Require UEFI Memory Attribute Table' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires UEFI firmware to publish a Memory Attributes Table (value 1) so firmware runtime memory is marked non-executable or read-only. HVCI relies on the MAT to extend code-integrity and memory protections over firmware regions; without it HVCI cannot constrain firmware memory, leaving a gap that could be used to bypass kernel code integrity. Setting 0 permits HVCI to run on firmware lacking these guarantees.
Change Risk Level: Func:L / Sec:H — HVCI related setting - we do not toggle it.

Change Risk Level: Func:M / Sec:M — Lockout policy; aggressive settings may lock out service accounts
